headline: High: Devin’s broad workspace and write/network privileges can collide with marketingskills’ shared-context file patterns, creating default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and action cascades.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, browser content, MCP outputs, and shared integrations by default, while marketingskills explicitly uses shared-context skill files and references that can be built on. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if marketing content or shared files are treated as trusted. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF marketingskills content is copied into Devin’s workspace or MCP inputs as instructions
IF Devin parses shared skill files or marketing drafts as authoritative prompts
mitigations: Restrict Devin to read-only ingestion for marketingskills artifacts
Add a provenance banner to shared skill files
Separate instruction files from content files
Disable MCP sources that can inject untrusted text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and prompt-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and integration tokens in a cloud workspace with broad egress; marketingskills reads and writes local skill/context files. If the pair shares a workspace or synced repo, sensitive Devin context can flow into marketing outputs or external APIs. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible but not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or synced workspace
IF Devin’s integration tokens or team chat content are present in files marketingskills can read
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared repo before running either agent
Limit Devin’s egress to approved destinations only
Mark marketing context files as non-sensitive
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and secret scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use broad network egress; marketingskills can also read/write files and spawn subprocesses. On a shared repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Because both agents have overlapping write surfaces and no locking is documented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout or workspace directory
IF either agent performs writes without an external lock
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Serialize write access with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent during the other’s run
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on outputs, while marketingskills is a shared-context skill system that can produce reusable marketing content. If Devin consumes marketingskills output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or published material. The pathway exists in default-style workflows, but direct action authority is not fully evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Devin uses marketingskills output as a source of facts or copy without review
IF generated marketing text is forwarded into publishing, tickets, or commits
mitigations: Require human review before publishing
Add a verification checklist for sourced claims
Separate draft generation from execution steps
Tag unverified outputs in the workspace
requires-engineering: add citation and fact-check gates

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches team chat, issue trackers, docs, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, while marketingskills is an open-source skill repo with marketing content only. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to policy gaps if sensitive Devin data is copied into the marketing repo. I cite both because the risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential Devin data is placed into marketingskills files
IF the organization requires residency or retention controls not enforced by the shared repo
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the marketing repo
Review retention settings for shared files
Use redacted examples only
Document allowed data classes for each agent
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
